chunks: Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. 'Amir narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah b. 'Amir, from Ibrahim b. Abi Mahmud. He said: al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, Muharram is a month in which the people of the Jahiliyya would prohibit fighting, but our blood was deemed lawful in it, our sanctity was violated in it, our offspring and our women were taken captive in it, fires were set ablaze in our tents, and what was in them of our belongings was plundered, and the sanctity of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) was not observed in our affair.

Indeed, the day of al-Husayn wounded our eyelids, made our tears flow, and humiliated our beloved, in the land of suffering and affliction. It bequeathed us suffering and affliction until the day of termination. So upon the like of al-Husayn let those who weep, weep, for indeed weeping diminishes the great sins.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: My father (blessings of God upon him), when the month of Muharram would enter, would not be seen laughing, and intense grief would overcome him until ten days had passed from it. And when it was the tenth day, that day would be the day of his affliction and his mourning and his weeping, and he would say: It is the day in which al-Husayn (blessings of God upon him) was killed.

key_terms.البكاء: Weeping — given spiritual significance as an act that reduces great sins when done in remembrance of Imam Husayn's martyrdom
key_terms.الجاهلية: Jahiliyya — the pre-Islamic period of ignorance, used here to contrast how even the pre-Islamic Arabs honored the sacred month while the Umayyads did not
key_terms.الكآبة: Intense grief — describing the state of Imam Musa al-Kadhim during Muharram
key_terms.المحرم: Muharram — the first month of the Islamic calendar, one of the four sacred months in which fighting was prohibited even in pre-Islamic Arabia

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about mourning Imam Husayn during Muharram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) delivers a powerful lamentation about the tragedy of Karbala during the month of Muharram, describing how the sanctity of that sacred month was violated when the family of the Prophet was massacred. He emphasizes that weeping for Imam Husayn (AS) diminishes great sins, and describes how his father, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), would be consumed by grief during the first ten days of Muharram, reaching its peak on Ashura.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (rh) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. `Amer narrated to us from his uncle `Abdullah b. `Amer from Ibrahim b. Abi Mahmud.  He said: al-Rida (as) said:

Muharram is the month in which the people of the Jahiliyya would prohibit fighting, but our blood was deemed lawful in it, our sanctity was violated in it, our offspring and our women were made captives in it, fire was ignited in our marquees and what was in them of our provision was plundered. And (despite our relationship) to the Messenger of Allah (s), the sanctity in our affair was not observed.

Surely, on the day of Husayn, our eyelids were wounded, our tears made to flow, our beloved abased in the land of suffering and affliction. Suffering and affliction were rained down on us. So, those who lament should lament on the like of Husain till the day of termination (i.e. the last day of this world), for surely the crying diminishes the great sins.

Then, he (as) said: When the month of Muharram would enter, my father (as) would not be seen laughing, and intense grief would overcome him until ten days had passed from it. So, when it would be the tenth day, that day would be the day of his affliction and his mourning and his lamenting. And he would say: This is the day on which Husayn (as) was killed.
